Petitioner above-named who is in custody since 21.01.2023 has moved this Court
for grant of regular bail in connection with Jamua P.S. Case No.23 of 2023 registered under Sections
366A, 509 & 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 12 of Pocso Act.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that the case was registered for an offence of kidnapping and the victim had left her parents' house on her own accord and there was no enticement or inducement on the part of the petitioner.
However, as an after-thought, allegation of rape has also been made.
It is submitted that she had left her home on 18.01.2023 and returned on 19.01.2023.
It is submitted that independent witnesses have stated during investigation that there was love-affair between petitioner and the victim for the last two years.
It is further submitted that the victim-girl had refused for the medical examination.
Learned APP for the State assisted by learned counsel for the informant has vehemently opposed the prayer.
It is submitted that victim-girl is a minor and her consent is immaterial at any stage.
It is submitted that the victim girl has supported her case in the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr. P.C. and further charge- sheet has also been filed under Section 376 IPC.
Considering the submissions of learned counsel and the fact as discussed above, the bail application is allowed.

Accordingly, the petitioner named above shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the Rahul Kumar Das vs The State Of Jharkhand.
